proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{st})_{s,t})\), let
\(\mathcal Z=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\), and let \(\mathcal U\) be the
sigma-field generated jointly by all untreated responses and all treated event
outcomes.  Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} says, conditional
on \(z_0\), that \(\mathcal Z\) is independent of
\(\mathcal X\vee\mathcal U\).  Thus, for \(A\in\mathcal Z\) and
\(D\in\mathcal U\), the tower property and conditional independence give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(A\cap D\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 &=E[\mathbf 1_D E(\mathbf 1_A\mid z_0,\mathcal X,\mathcal U)
       \mid z_0,\mathcal X]\\
 &=E[\mathbf 1_D P(A\mid z_0)\mid z_0,\mathcal X]\\
 &=P(A\mid z_0)P(D\mid z_0,\mathcal X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-independence} makes the first factor the product
of the \(N\) one-donor conditional kernels.  Assumption
\texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes the second factor a product over
the joint within-unit histories indexed by \((s,i)\).  It does not split the
pre-event and event coordinates within one such history.

The latter qualification is substantive and remains true after adding
\texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.  For example, condition on an exact
design, take independent centered Rademacher variables \(U_{si}\) across
\((s,i)\), and, for a sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), set
\[
 Q_{s1i}=m_s(X_{s1})+\varepsilon U_{si},
 \qquad
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b_s+\varepsilon U_{si}.
\]
Use fresh independent centered bounded errors in the other windows.  Then
\(E[Q_{s1i}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{s1})\) and
\(E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=b_s
=E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]\), while the two displayed variables are
dependent conditional on \((z_0,\mathcal X)\).  The support restriction is
preserved by taking \(\varepsilon\) small, and the corresponding potential
outcomes can be centered to satisfy event-date transport and consistency.
Hence no stronger within-unit product factorization follows.

Finally, \texttt{ass:center-only-design} places the exact \(X_{st}\), not a
noisy surrogate, in \(\mathcal X\).  Therefore the response kernel is
conditioned directly on its regression coordinate; there is no measurement-
error convolution and hence no deconvolution operator on a training
coordinate.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), and a
feasible \(u=(u_1^{\top},\ldots,u_S^{\top})^{\top}\) satisfying
\(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2\le\delta\).  By
\texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity},
\[
 \|u\|_2^2
 =\|\Sigma^{1/2}\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2^2
 \le\lambda_{\max}(\Sigma)\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2^2
 \le C_\Sigma\delta^2.
\]
Let \(C_{\mathrm{Hol}}\) be the finite norm-equivalence constant determined
by the stated isotropic Holder convention.  Assumption
\texttt{ass:holder-regression} implies
\[
 |m_s(x+v)-m_s(x)|
 \le C_{\mathrm{Hol}}L\|v\|_2^\kappa,
 \qquad \kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\},
\]
whenever both arguments lie in \([0,1]^d\).  For
\(0<\lambda\le1\) this is the defining Holder inequality.  For
\(\lambda>1\), the Holder-ball bound on the first derivatives and the
fundamental theorem of calculus along the line segment from \(x\) to \(x+v\)
give the displayed Lipschitz inequality.

Since \(\pi_s>0\), \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), and
\(\|u_s\|_2\le\|u\|_2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
   \{m_s(z_{0s}+u_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
 &\le C_{\mathrm{Hol}}L\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\|u_s\|_2^\kappa\\
 &\le C_{\mathrm{Hol}}L C_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\delta^\kappa.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking the supremum over the feasible set in
\texttt{def:local-modulus} proves the upper inequality with
\(C=C_{\mathrm{Hol}}LC_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\).  The lower inequality is
exactly \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}.  Combining the two proves
\[
 c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa
 \le\omega_P(\delta;z_0)
 \le C\delta^\kappa.
\]

Put \(A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2/n_s\).  We construct two laws whose exact
training-design, training-response, and donor kernels agree.  The displayed
richness compatibility permits a bounded affine surface when \(\kappa=1\),
or an asymmetric \(\kappa\)-cusp when \(\kappa<1\), with Holder norm and range
strictly inside the respective \(L\) and \(B\) bounds and with standardized
modulus constant at least \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\).  Center such a surface so that
\(m_s(z_{0s})=0\), take \(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\), and use any donor
kernel satisfying the stated unbiasedness, ellipticity, and fourth-moment
bounds.  Set \(B_{si}(0)=0\).  These choices satisfy event-date transport,
design-conditional centering for the training responses, and all observation-
structure conditions.

Fix \(b\in(0,B]\).  For \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), let
\(B_{si}(1)\in\{-b,b\}\) be independent across \((s,i)\), independent of
the design and donors, with
\[
 P_v\{B_{si}(1)=b\}=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{b n_s\sqrt A},
\]
where \(\gamma>0\) is fixed and sufficiently small.  Along the stated growth
arrays, \(|\varepsilon_s|\le1/4\).  Set
\(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\).  Consistency holds, and
\(E_v[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,\mathcal X]=2vb\varepsilon_s
=E_v[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]\), so the repaired centering assumption
also holds.  All support and cross-unit independence requirements are
preserved.  By \texttt{def:target}, the target separation is
\[
 \Delta:=|\tau_{P_1}(z_0)-\tau_{P_{-1}}(z_0)|
 =4b\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\varepsilon_s
 =4\gamma\sqrt A.
\]

The Hellinger affinity of the two one-observation sign laws in cohort \(s\)
is
\[
 \sqrt{(1/2+\varepsilon_s)(1/2-\varepsilon_s)}
 +\sqrt{(1/2-\varepsilon_s)(1/2+\varepsilon_s)}
 =\sqrt{1-4\varepsilon_s^2}.
\]
Independence across units therefore makes the affinity of the two complete
event samples
\[
 \mathcal A
 =\prod_{s=1}^{S}(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge \exp\!\left(-8\sum_s n_s\varepsilon_s^2\right)
 =\exp(-8\gamma^2/b^2),
\]
where \(\log(1-x)\ge-2x\) for \(0\le x\le1/2\) was used.  If \(p_1,p_{-1}\)
are densities with respect to a common dominating measure, Cauchy--Schwarz
gives
\[
 \|P_1-P_{-1}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 =\frac12\int|\sqrt{p_1}-\sqrt{p_{-1}}|
                 (\sqrt{p_1}+\sqrt{p_{-1}})
 \le\sqrt{1-\mathcal A^2}.
\]
Choose \(\gamma\) so that the right side is at most \(1/2\).

For an arbitrary estimator, assign it to the closer of the two target values.
On every testing error its squared estimation error is at least
\(\Delta^2/4\).  Integrating the pointwise minimum of the two densities gives
\[
 \max_{v\in\{-1,1\}}E_{P_v}
   [\{\widetilde\tau-\tau_{P_v}(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}
      \{1-\|P_1-P_{-1}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\}
 \ge\gamma^2 A.
\]
The construction is independent of the realized exact design, so the last
bound holds for every such array.  Taking the infimum over estimators and the
supremum over the model class proves the claim with \(c=\gamma^2\).

Let
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad
 D_T=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{2\lambda/d},
 \qquad
 D_N=N^{-\kappa}.
\]
The treated-mean two-point construction in the proof of the narrowed
\texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} has target separation proportional to
\(A^{1/2}\) and total variation bounded strictly below one.  The elementary
nearest-target test used there therefore gives a marginal squared-risk lower
bound \(c_1A\).

For the donor channel, \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} supplies
two laws whose centers are separated by order \(N^{-1/2}\), whose total
variation is bounded strictly below one, and whose targets are separated by
at least \(c_2N^{-\kappa/2}\).  The same nearest-target test gives the lower
bound \(c_3D_N\).

The block-label construction in
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies two laws whose
observed distributions possess a common subprobability measure of fixed
positive mass, while their targets are separated by \(c_4D_T^{1/2}\).  The
nearest-target test consequently yields \(c_5D_T\).

Finally, for \(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\),
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.
\]
Because \(S\) is fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left[\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right]^2
 \le2S A+2T^{-2\lambda/d}
 \le C(A+D_T).
\]
Thus the corrected \(R_\star\) is bounded above, up to a fixed constant, by
\(A\vee D_T\vee D_N\).  Selecting the two-point subexperiment corresponding
to the largest of these three entries proves the claimed lower bound.

We first record an elementary interval inequality.  Suppose two observed laws
\(P_0,P_1\), with target values \(\theta_0,\theta_1\), possess a common
subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta\).  If an interval \(I\) has
coverage at least \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under each law, then
\[
 \nu\{\theta_v\in I\}\ge\eta-\alpha-o(1),\qquad v=0,1.
\]
The union bound within \(\nu\) gives
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}\ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).
\]
Consequently, whenever \(\eta>2\alpha\),
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}E_{P_v}[\operatorname{length}(I)]
 \ge |\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
We apply (1) to three subexperiments.

For the treated-mean channel, use the two sign laws constructed in the proof
of the narrowed \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}.  Their target separation is
\(4\gamma\{\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\}^{1/2}\).  By choosing \(\gamma\) still
smaller, their total variation distance is less than \(1-2\alpha\).  The
measure with density \(\min(p_0,p_1)\) is then a common subprobability measure
of mass exceeding \(2\alpha\).  Equation (1) yields
\[
 \sup_P E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \ge c_1\left\{\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}\right\}^{1/2}.
 \tag{2}
\]

For the donor channel, choose the separation constant in
\texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} small enough that its common
subprobability mass exceeds \(2\alpha\).  Applying (1) to that family gives
\[
 \sup_P E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \ge c_3N^{-\kappa/2}.
 \tag{3}
\]

For the spacing channel,
\texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies a common
subprobability mass greater than \(2\alpha\) and target separation of order
\(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{\lambda/d}\).  Equation (1) therefore gives
\[
 \sup_P E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \ge c_5\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
 \tag{4}
\]

It remains only to compare these three bounds with the corrected definition.
For each cohort put \(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Direct
algebra gives
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed and \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), Cauchy--Schwarz yields
\[
 \left[\sum_s\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right]^2
 \le2S\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}+2T^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
The last term is bounded by a fixed multiple of
\(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\).  Hence the square root of the corrected
\(R_\star\) is, up to constants depending only on fixed class parameters, the
maximum of the right sides of (2)--(4).  Taking the corresponding
subexperiment for the largest entry proves the asserted lower bound.

The omitted upper assertion for \(C_\alpha\) is not a consequence of this
argument.  In particular, boundedness alone does not make a Wald statistic
uniformly asymptotically normal.

added_lemmas.statement:
If \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\), there are constants
\(c_0>0\) and \(\eta_0>0\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such
that for all sufficiently large \(N\) the model class
contains two laws whose realized interior paths are separated by order
\(N^{-1/2}\), whose observed-data total variation distance is at most
\(1-\eta_0\), and whose causal targets are separated by at least
\(c_0N^{-\kappa/2}\).  The training and treated-event observed laws can be
chosen identical; only the donor-location experiment and the transported
untreated potential mean differ.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
It is enough to vary one coordinate.  Put
\(z_0^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\) and
\(z_0^{(1)}=z_0^{(0)}+\delta_Ne_1\), where
\(\delta_N=c_*N^{-1/2}\) and \(c_*>0\) will be chosen small.  Both paths are
at distance at least \(\delta_0\) from the boundary for all large \(N\).

Choose fixed support points \(x_-<1/2<x_+\) for the first donor coordinate.
Under law \(v\), choose its success probability so that its mean is the first
coordinate of \(z_0^{(v)}\).  Thus the two success probabilities differ by
\(\delta_N/(x_+-x_-)\) and remain in \([1/4,3/4]\).  Give the other donor
coordinates common independent symmetric two-point laws.  Scaling the fixed
support spacings makes every covariance eigenvalue lie in
\([c_\Sigma,C_\Sigma]\).  Jensen's inequality shows that nonemptiness of the
frozen fourth-moment class requires \(B^4\ge(Sd)^2\); symmetric two-point
coordinates attain this lower order, and the small probability perturbation
keeps the standardized fourth moment below the fixed envelope for all large
\(N\).  Hence donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, and the fourth-moment condition
hold.

For probabilities in \([1/4,3/4]\), direct differentiation of
\(\sqrt{pq}+\sqrt{(1-p)(1-q)}\) gives a constant \(C_0\) such that the
one-donor Hellinger affinity is at least
\(1-C_0\delta_N^2\).  Independence of the donors gives product affinity at
least \((1-C_0\delta_N^2)^N\ge e^{-2C_0c_*^2}\).  The Cauchy--Schwarz
calculation in the proof of the narrowed conditional theorem then gives
\[
 \|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\{1-e^{-4C_0c_*^2}\}^{1/2}.
\]
Choosing \(c_*\) small makes this at most \(1-\eta_0\) for a fixed
\(\eta_0>0\).

Use a common exact uniform training design and deterministic responses
\(Q_{sti}=m_s(X_{st})\).  If \(\kappa=1\), choose a sufficiently small bounded
affine first-coordinate component with nonzero slope.  If
\(0<\kappa<1\), choose, on the first cohort and coordinate,
\[
 m_1(x)=a|x_1-z_{01}^{(0)}|^\kappa
       +2a|x_1-z_{01}^{(1)}|^\kappa
\]
and take the other surfaces constant.  A sufficiently small fixed \(a>0\)
places these surfaces in the stated Holder ball.  At \(z_0^{(0)}\), moving in
the negative first-coordinate direction produces an increment of magnitude at
least \(a|u|^\kappa\); at \(z_0^{(1)}\), moving in the positive direction
produces an increment of magnitude at least \(2a|u|^\kappa\).  Ellipticity
converts these coordinate displacements to covariance-standardized
displacements by fixed factors.  Thus both laws satisfy the attainable local
modulus after choosing \(a\) with the required fixed slack.  Moreover,
\[
 |m_1(z_{01}^{(1)})-m_1(z_{01}^{(0)})|
 =a\delta_N^\kappa.
\]
Take identical deterministic treated observed outcomes under the two laws,
set \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\), and choose the unobserved
\(B_{si}(0)\) to have mean \(m_s(z_{0s}^{(v)})\).  This verifies consistency,
event-date transport, both design-conditional centering equalities, and all
support conditions after the common amplitudes are chosen small.  By
\texttt{def:target}, the two targets are separated by a fixed multiple of
\(\delta_N^\kappa=N^{-\kappa/2}\).  The training and observed event laws are
identical, so the preceding donor total-variation bound proves the claim.
added_lemmas.justification: This two-law family is the computable donor-location certificate behind the \(N^{-\kappa}\) MSE and \(N^{-\kappa/2}\) honest-length converses.
added_lemmas.gap: The lower modulus alone is not a testing experiment; the lemma supplies overlapping donor laws and verifies the causal-class embedding.
added_lemmas.consumer: The marginal MSE and honest-length lower bounds both use this family.

added_lemmas.statement:
If \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\), then for every
\(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\) there are constants \(c_\alpha>0\) and
\(\eta_\alpha>2\alpha\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(T\), the
model class contains two laws with the same interior realized path whose
observed-data laws possess a common subprobability measure of mass at least
\(\eta_\alpha\), while their causal targets differ by at least
\[
 c_\alpha\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\]
Both laws satisfy the frozen geometric beta-mixing envelope and the repaired
design-conditional centering assumption.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Choose \(\gamma>0\) so that \(e^{-\gamma}>2\alpha\).  Let
\[
 L_T=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\log T-2\log\log(T\vee3)}{|\log\rho_0|}
 \right\rfloor\vee1,
 \qquad p_T=\frac{\gamma L_T}{T}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(T\), decreasing \(\gamma\) if necessary gives
\(2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}\).  Partition
\(\{1,\ldots,T\}\) into consecutive deterministic blocks of length
\(L_T\), ignoring a final incomplete block.  Independently label every
complete block by \(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).

Let \(A_T\) be a cube centered at \(z_0\) and having volume \(p_T\).
Conditional on \(C_b=1\), draw the design points in block \(b\) independently
uniformly on \(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently
uniformly on its complement.  The incomplete block may be drawn independently
uniformly on the cube.  At every complete-block time the marginal density is
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf 1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf 1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\]
A past and future sigma-field separated by \(k<L_T\) can share only one block
label.  Coupling that label to an independent copy fails with probability at
most \(2p_T\), so \(\beta(k)\le2p_T\).  If \(k\ge L_T\), the two sigma-fields
involve disjoint independent block labels and \(\beta(k)=0\).  Hence
\(\beta(k)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\) for every \(k\ge1\).

Let \(E_T\) be the event that every complete block has label zero.  Then
\[
 P(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}
 \longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}=:\eta_\alpha>2\alpha,
\]
and no complete-block design point lies in \(A_T\).  Shrinking the cube by a
fixed factor, if necessary, removes the independent incomplete block without
changing its order; equivalently include the incomplete block in \(E_T\),
which changes its probability by \(o(1)\).

Write \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\).  Let
\[
 \phi(y)=e\,\exp\{-1/(1-\|y\|_2^2)\}\mathbf 1\{\|y\|_2<1\}.
\]
This function is infinitely differentiable, supported on the unit ball, and
satisfies \(\phi(0)=1\).  Therefore
\(h_T^\lambda\phi((x-z_0)/h_T)\) has a Holder-\(\lambda\) norm bounded by a
constant independent of \(T\).  Start with a bounded affine surface when
\(\kappa=1\), or an asymmetric \(\kappa\)-cusp when
\(0<\kappa<1\), whose covariance-standardized attainable modulus has a fixed
strict margin above \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\).  For a sufficiently small fixed
\(a>0\), put
\[
 m_0=m_{\mathrm{base}},
 \qquad
 m_1=m_{\mathrm{base}}+a h_T^\lambda
        \phi((\,cdot-z_0)/h_T).
\]
Holder scaling and the strict margin show that both laws satisfy
\texttt{ass:holder-regression} and
\texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}; all values remain inside the wealth
support.

Set \(Q_{ti}=m_v(X_t)\), take identical donors and identical treated observed
outcomes, impose consistency, and choose the unobserved untreated event mean
to equal \(m_v(z_0)\).  Conditional response centering and treated-mean
centering are then exact.  On \(E_T\), every observed response is evaluated
outside the bump support, so the two complete observed laws coincide.  Their
restrictions to \(E_T\) define a common subprobability measure of mass tending
to \(\eta_\alpha\).  Event-date transport and \texttt{def:target} give
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|
 =a h_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\]
This proves the asserted two-law certificate.
added_lemmas.justification: This explicit rare-cluster process proves that geometric beta mixing by itself does not deliver the iid pointwise spacing law uniformly over triangular arrays.
added_lemmas.gap: Ordinary iid random-design spacing arguments do not control state-dependent clustering of a shrinking target neighborhood.
added_lemmas.consumer: The corrected marginal and honest-length lower bounds use its common-submeasure certificate.

added_lemmas.statement:
After a total feasible interval attaining the corrected geometric-mixing rate
has been constructed, can its conditional expected length attain the exact
asymptotic minimax constant simultaneously at every intersection of the
remaining sampling phases while estimating the full donor covariance and the
calendar long-run variance?  The handle is the product-experiment ordered-
modulus construction in \texttt{def:sharp-constant-handle}, with least-
favorable tests calibrated only after the moving-center Gram and rare-set
anti-clustering problems are controlled.
added_lemmas.justification: Exact constants are downstream of a valid order-optimal upper construction and cannot be settled by the obsolete uncentered-class witness.
added_lemmas.gap: The product experiment has random local geometry, rare-set clustering under beta mixing, a Holder donor location, and estimated dependence.
added_lemmas.consumer: A future exact-constant result would guide resource allocation at intersections of the corrected sampling phases.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under \texttt{ass:event-date-transport},
\texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, and
\texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, suppose in addition that
\[
 c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256.
\]
Then there is a constant \(c>0\), depending only on the fixed class
parameters, such that for every growth array, every interior realized path
\(z_0\), and every exact design array,
\[
 c\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
 \le
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})].
\]
No conditional upper bound for the particular estimator \(\widehat\tau\) is
asserted under the sole realized-design condition \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The every-design upper bound is false even after design-conditional centering. In the scalar \(\lambda=1\) model, put only order \(T/\sqrt N\) exact design points near \(z_0\) and the remainder near a remote point. Then \(g_{1T}(z_0)=O(N^{-1/2})\) and \(R_D=O(N^{-1})\), but a donor-fold mean lies several \(N^{-1/2}\) units to one side with probability bounded away from zero. The first-coercive rule then skips the local cluster and fits the remote cluster, producing constant conditional squared error. The retained treated-mean lower bound is a genuine consequence of the original claim and is proved here.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under the regular random-design law, \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering},
and \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, suppose
\(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\).  Then there is a constant \(c>0\),
depending only on the fixed class parameters, such that
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0]\ge cR_\star,
\]
with \(R_\star\) given by the corrected geometric-mixing construction in
\texttt{def:marginal-rate}.  The \(N^{-\kappa}\) component of this converse
uses the attainable-direction restriction.  No matching upper bound over the
full beta-mixing class is asserted until the open anti-clustering problem is
discharged.  On the independent-calendar subclass the spacing lower-bound
construction has order \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The claimed equivalence is too strong because the beta-mixing envelope permits shrinking neighborhoods to occur in blocks of length proportional to \(\log T\). The explicit common-submeasure construction proves a \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\) MSE lower bound. This bundle corrects the rate construction and retains the proved minimax lower half; the matching upper half remains a genuine research obligation.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under \texttt{ass:event-date-transport},
\texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, and
\texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}, suppose
\(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\).  Then every sequence of
data-measurable random intervals \(I_\alpha\) satisfying
\[
 \liminf\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 P_P\{\tau(z_0)\in I_\alpha\mid z_0\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
obeys
\[
 \liminf\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)\mid z_0]
 \ge cR_\star^{1/2},

\texttt{def:marginal-rate}.  No coverage or upper expected-length assertion is

If treated increments are Bernoulli with probability \(\gamma/n\), then with probability tending to \(e^{-\gamma}\) all treated observations are zero and their sample variance is zero. Taking \(T\) and \(N\) sufficiently large makes every added bias radius \(o(n^{-1})\), so the interval misses the target \(\gamma/n\). The lower expected-length half remains valid at the corrected rate and is proved here.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A feasible estimator upper bound matching the corrected \(R_\star\) uniformly over the full geometrically beta-mixing triangular-array class.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen no-log spacing rate is false: shrinking neighborhoods may occur in dependent blocks of length proportional to \(\log T\) while still satisfying \(\beta(k)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\). The old route of averaging the local \(N^{-1/2}\)-tube conditional scale also fails on generated centers outside that tube.
open_obligations.attempted: I tested iid nearest-neighbor/local-polynomial arguments, covariance bounds for rare-ball counts, deterministic calendar blocking, and the frozen first-coercive bandwidth rule. The iid route yields \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\), but beta-mixing blocking necessarily exposes the rare-cluster logarithm; the frozen conditional rule has a separate remote-cluster counterexample.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The no-log spacing term is false under the frozen beta-mixing condition.  It
already fails for \(S=d=1\).  Let \(z_0=1/2\), and let \(L_T\) be an integer
of order \(\log T/|\log\rho_0|\), chosen slightly smaller so that, with
\(p_T=\gamma L_T/T\),
\[
 2p_T\le\beta_0\rho_0^{L_T-1}.
\]
Partition the calendar deterministically into blocks of length \(L_T\).  Give
each block an independent label \(C_b\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_T)\).
Let \(A_T\) be a cube centered at \(z_0\) of volume \(p_T\).  Conditional on
\(C_b=1\), draw every \(X_t\) in that block independently uniformly on
\(A_T\); conditional on \(C_b=0\), draw them independently uniformly on
\([0,1]^d\setminus A_T\).  Each \(X_t\) is exactly uniform because
\[
 p_T\frac{\mathbf 1_{A_T}(x)}{p_T}
 +(1-p_T)\frac{\mathbf 1_{A_T^c}(x)}{1-p_T}=1.
\]
Past and future can share at most one block label.  Consequently
\(\beta(k)\le2p_T\) for \(k<L_T\) and \(\beta(k)=0\) for \(k\ge L_T\), so
the displayed geometric envelope holds.  Nevertheless, the event \(E_T\)
that no block is labeled one has probability
\[
 P(E_T)=(1-p_T)^{\lfloor T/L_T\rfloor}\longrightarrow e^{-\gamma}>0,
\]
and on \(E_T\) no design point enters \(A_T\).

Let \(h_T\asymp p_T^{1/d}\), and take a smooth bump
\(\phi_T(x)=h_T^\lambda\phi((x-z_0)/h_T)\), where \(\phi\) is supported on
the unit ball, \(\phi(0)=1\), and its fixed Holder norm is finite.  Start from
a bounded surface with an attainable direction having slack, and define
\(m_1=m_0+c\phi_T\) for a sufficiently small fixed \(c>0\).  Holder scaling
keeps both surfaces in \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and the slack preserves
the lower local modulus.  Take \(Q_{ti}=m_v(X_t)\), identical treated observed
outcomes under the two laws, transported untreated event outcomes with means
\(m_v(z_0)\), and identical donors.  All repaired conditional-centering
equalities hold.  On \(E_T\), the two complete observed laws agree, whereas
\[
 |\tau_1(z_0)-\tau_0(z_0)|=c h_T^\lambda
 \asymp\left\{\frac{\log T}{T}\right\}^{\lambda/d}.
\]
The elementary two-point testing inequality therefore yields
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0]
 \ge c'\left\{\frac{\log T}{T}\right\}^{2\lambda/d}.
\]
Taking \(n_s\) and \(N\) sufficiently large makes every other old entry
\(o(T^{-2\lambda/d}\log(T)^{2\lambda/d})\).  Thus averaging the old
 conditional expression cannot prove the frozen no-log marginal claim.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A total feasible interval attaining the corrected expected-length rate under bounded outcomes, including the spacing regime with only finitely many locally informative calendar blocks.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen normal critical value and centered block-sample variance are not uniformly valid when the variance degenerates or when only finitely many local blocks carry weight. Rare treated outcomes give a direct undercoverage sequence even with iid calendars and exact affine regression.
open_obligations.attempted: I separated donor bias, Holder bias, treated sampling noise, and calendar scores, and checked the full-range branches. None of those branches is triggered when all rare treated increments are zero, so the Wald radius remains too small. A concentration-based or replicate-aware interval requires a new construction rather than another proof of the frozen formula.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The stated interval \(C_\alpha\) is not uniformly honest.  Take
\(S=d=1\), \(z_0=1/2\), \(\lambda>1\), and a bounded affine regression
\(m(x)=c+a(x-z_0)\) with \(a\ne0\).  Put \(Q_{ti}=m(X_t)\) and use independent
uniform designs, so every regular local-linear fit recovers \(m\) exactly.
Let \(B_i(0)=c\) and
\[
 B_i(1)=B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=c+V_i,
 \qquad V_i\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\gamma/n).
\]
Then consistency, transport, boundedness, cross-unit independence, and both
design-conditional centering equalities hold, and
\(\tau(z_0)=\gamma/n\).  Choose \(T\) and \(N\) to grow sufficiently faster
than \(n\) that the selected-bandwidth Holder term and the donor term in
\(R_\alpha\), as well as the donor displacement of the fitted affine
regression, are \(o(n^{-1})\) with probability tending to one.  The calendar
residual scores are zero on the regular branch.  On the event
\(V_1=\cdots=V_n=0\), whose probability tends to \(e^{-\gamma}\), the treated
sample variance is zero and the center and radius of \(C_\alpha\) are both
\(o(n^{-1})\).  Therefore \(\gamma/n\notin C_\alpha\) on that event for all
large \(n\).  Choosing \(\gamma\) with \(e^{-\gamma}>\alpha\) gives
\[
 \limsup P\{\tau(z_0)\in C_\alpha\mid z_0\}
 \le1-e^{-\gamma}<1-\alpha.
\]
This is a failure of the Wald construction, not of causal transport.

prose_updates.tldr: The causal target remains cohort-weighted buy-and-hold level wealth at a fixed realized event path, identified by consistency and the explicitly untestable event-date transport equality. Exact historical paths and an independent generated event center still imply a Holder location modulus rather than deconvolution, and the repaired design-conditional centering condition removes the earlier common-design mean shock. It does not, however, validate the frozen positive frontiers: the conditional Gram radius controls too small a donor tube, geometric beta mixing permits a logarithmic rare-neighborhood clustering penalty, and the proposed Wald interval is not uniformly honest for rare bounded outcomes. This round proves the sigma-field factorization, the two-sided modulus, the treated-mean conditional lower bound, and corrected log-aware marginal MSE and honest-length lower bounds; matching feasible upper constructions and exact constants remain open.

project_justification.fill: The project cleanly separates causal transport, observed-law centering, exact training coordinates, and generated-center uncertainty. The proved contribution at this stage is a donor-versus-joint-panel factorization, a full-covariance two-sided Holder modulus, and explicit testing certificates for treated replication, donor location, and geometrically mixing design spacing. The last certificate shows that the worst-case spacing entry under the frozen beta-mixing triangular arrays is \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\), while iid calendars recover \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\). The displayed local-polynomial estimator and calendar-block Wald interval remain samplewise defined candidates, but their claimed uniform upper guarantees are not established.

sampling_model.design: For each fixed cohort, every exact pre-event path has a density bounded above and away from zero on \([0,1]^d\). Geometric beta mixing controls fixed-lag dependence but, for triangular arrays, still permits visits to a shrinking neighborhood to arrive in blocks of length proportional to \(\log T\); an iid or explicit small-ball anti-clustering condition is needed for the no-log pointwise spacing rate.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The event path is the mean of \(N\) independent donor scores with unknown full covariance. Projection, spectral clipping, a finite bandwidth grid, and fallback rules make the estimator total, but the current realized Gram radius controls only centers within \(N^{-1/2}\) of the true path. A fold mean exits that fixed-radius tube with nonvanishing probability, so a valid conditional frontier must incorporate the full generated-center geometry rather than treating every such sample as regular.

prose_updates.related_work: Stone (1982), Fan (1993), and Fan et al. (1997) give iid or ordinary random-design local-polynomial benchmarks, not uniform small-ball hitting rates for triangular arrays under beta mixing. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) and Hahn and Ridder (2013) perturb generated training coordinates, whereas the present exact-training experiment perturbs only the query location. Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) and Fan and Truong (1993) study contaminated training coordinates and deconvolution. Donoho (1994), Low (1997), and Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) motivate modulus and bias-aware inference, but they do not certify the frozen Wald construction under rare outcomes or finitely many locally informative blocks. Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide dependent synthetic-control prediction tools; an additional anti-clustering or concentration argument is still needed for the corrected upper frontier here.
prose_updates.interpretation: Design-conditional centering is necessary but not sufficient for the advertised rates. Applied users must separately justify how often the historical path process visits shrinking neighborhoods of the realized event path and must use inference that remains valid when outcome variances or the number of locally informative calendar blocks are small. Donor uncertainty remains a location-modulus problem because the historical coordinates themselves are exact.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The deleted common-design-shock nodes concerned the larger class obtained by removing design-conditional centering and are not theorems about the repaired class. New in-class witnesses expose different limitations. First, an \(N^{-1/2}\)-tube Gram condition does not control all foldwise donor centers with sufficiently small error probability. Second, geometric beta mixing alone permits rare-set clusters and forces a \(\log T\) spacing penalty in the worst triangular array. Third, a normal/Wald radius based on sample variances is not uniformly valid for rare bounded outcomes. A future positive result must replace the conditional geometry functional and the interval construction, or strengthen the sampling model with explicit primitive conditions.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The target remains causal only under event-date transport, while design-conditional centering remains a distinct observed-law restriction. The attainable-direction condition continues to be needed for the donor converse. Under the explicit richness compatibility \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\), the proved uniform claims are lower bounds: treated replication contributes \(\sum_s\pi_s^2/n_s\), donor location contributes \(N^{-\kappa}\), and worst-case beta-mixing spacing contributes \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\). The frozen estimator upper bound and Wald interval coverage are not valid as stated. The sharp-constant question is restored only as an unresolved downstream question after an order-optimal feasible upper construction is found.

statement_notes.gap: The original generated-center upper bound fails because its realized geometry is controlled only on a fixed-standard-error tube.
